Sonia Gandhi had personally expressed a desire to meet Lalu Yadav after learning that he was in Delhi for a medical check-up.

Tejashwi Yadav recalled the political association between Sonia Gandhi and Lalu Yadav during UPA era.

NEW DELHI: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi met RJD patriarch Lalu Prasad Yadav at the residence of his daughter, Misa Bharti, in New Delhi on Monday and enquired about his health as he continues to undergo treatment at AIIMS in the national capital.Lalu Prasad was recently brought to Delhi for specialised medical consultations after receiving treatment and remaining under observation at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (IGIMS) in Patna.His condition is currently stable, according to family members.Tejashwi Yadav , on social media platform X, recalled the political association between Sonia Gandhi and his father during the UPA government (2004-2014).He highlighted welfare initiatives undertaken during that period for farmers, young people, soldiers and the common public, as well as key legislations such as MGNREGA, the Right to Education (RTE) Act and the Right to Information (RTI) Act.He also pointed out that the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh 's government had allocated more than Rs 1.45 lakh crore for Bihar's development.The Bihar leader of the opposition said Sonia Gandhi, whose memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", is scheduled for release on November 10, had personally expressed a desire to meet his father after learning that he was in Delhi for a medical check-up."Lalu Prasad had come to Delhi for his routine medical check-up. I also met Sonia Gandhi and informed her about this. She herself expressed a desire to meet Lalu Prasad, which is why she visited him today. Lalu Prasad and Sonia Gandhi have shared a good relationship from the very beginning. They have stood by and supported each other during difficult circumstances. Our family and the Gandhi family have also shared a longstanding relationship. The purpose of today's meeting was to enquire about Lalu Prasad's health. They had not met for a long time, which is why they met today," Tejashwi wrote on X in Hindi.Lalu Yadav also posted about this meet with Sonia Gandhi on X, writing: "It was recalled how, during the days of the UPA government, we implemented transparent and public welfare schemes for the youth, farmers, soldiers, and the common man, and how the countrymen were empowered through laws like MGNREGA, RTE, and RTI. Under the leadership of Sardar Manmohan Singh ji, how we provided more than 1 lakh 45 thousand crore rupees for the development of Bihar. "Tejashwi also spoke about the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, saying opposition parties would need to remain united to take on the challenges facing the country.He said the gathering was not the end of the campaign against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and insisted that the opposition would continue pressing for action against him."We will not win this battle unless we stand united. We did gather yesterday, but that was not the final event. We are not the kind of people who will sit quietly until action is taken against Gyanesh Kumar," he said.The RJD leader also hit back at the BJP for describing the opposition rally as a failure. Questioning the ruling party's reaction, he alleged that the rally had unsettled the BJP."Why are they so nervous? If the rally had been a flop, why would there be any need to prove it was a flop? They know that there is unease and turmoil. They are troubled and disappointed because their theft has been exposed," he said.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi met RJD patriarch Lalu Prasad Yadav in New Delhi on Monday. She enquired about his health as he continues to undergo treatment at AIIMS. Tejashwi Yadav recalled the political association between Sonia Gandhi and his father during UPA era.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) alleged a rift within the Congress leadership, claiming that Rahul Gandhi 's camp was insecure about Priyanka Gandhi Vadra 's growing influence and was deliberately sidelining her within the party.BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress leadership of denying Priyanka Gandhi an opportunity to address the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. He also alleged that she was sidelined during the party's mock Parliament event held a day earlier.Also Read| '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption In a video statement, Bhandari claimed that the Congress was divided into two power centres, with Rahul Gandhi's camp allegedly attempting to limit his sister's political prominence."Priyanka Vadra, who has served as the General Secretary of the Congress Party and is Rahul Gandhi’s sister, was not allowed to speak today at the Ramlila Ground. Did Rahul Gandhi prevent her from speaking today? And not just today, even yesterday during the Mock Parliament, when Rahul Gandhi's relaunch exercise was taking place, Priyanka Vadra's chair was placed in the second row, and she was not allowed to speak there either," Bhandari said.Claiming that Rahul Gandhi's political team was apprehensive of Priyanka Gandhi's influence within the party, the BJP spokesperson accused the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha of prioritising internal political manoeuvring over public issues."The Rahul camp is insecure about the Priyanka camp, and the Priyanka camp is being suppressed. Rahul Gandhi, who is undergoing his hundredth relaunch, is not talking about the people of the country or about the Congress Party today; instead, he is merely trying to sideline Priyanka Gandhi Vadra," the BJP national spokesperson said.Taking another swipe at the Congress leadership, Bhandari said: "Between Rahul versus Priyanka, the Congress is divided into two factions, and the public is watching this fight while eating popcorn."The BJP's remarks came as Opposition leaders and supporters gathered at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi for the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' rally against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged irregularities in the exercise.The march began at the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction and proceeded towards Ramlila Maidan. The gathering followed a public mock impeachment programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar held in the national capital on October 31.Several Opposition leaders attended the rally, including Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress leader Mamata Banerjee, Abhishek Banerjee, Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy, National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, CPI leader D Raja, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav.The BJP's allegations centred on Priyanka Gandhi's absence from the list of speakers at the rally and her seating arrangement at the mock Parliament event. Bhandari did not provide independent evidence to establish that Rahul Gandhi had prevented his sister from addressing either gathering.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress leadership of denying Priyanka Gandhi an opportunity to address the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. He also alleged that she was sidelined during the party's mock Parliament event held a day earlier. The BJP did not provide independent evidence to establish that Rahul Gandhi prevented his sister from addressing either gathering.

Article Title: INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
Article Text:
Ramlila Maidan became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt

NEW DELHI: If the stage at Ramlila Maidan sent out a strong message of a united opposition that will not relent till it sees Gyanesh Kumar's removed as Chief Election Commissioner, the atmosphere at the packed grounds reflected the same sense of coming together as flags of all hues representing the diverse ideologies of INDIA parties were held up by workers and supporters.From slogans like "Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod" to the euphoric response of the crowd to repeated chanting of "Inquilab Zindabad" - the Ramlila Maidan on Sunday became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt. The RJD and Samajwadi Party flags shared space with a sea of flags representing the Left parties - a reflection of how diverse ideologies and ideas converged on ground for a common cause.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi got the loudest applause from the crowd that had been growing strong since 9 in the morning and remained eager to stay even as the main speeches only took off at 3 pm as the top leaders of the INDIA parties arrived on stage after the Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao March from CP Minto Road Junction to the rally venue.With 2027 set to see crucial assembly polls in UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand, one saw Samajwadi Party supporters assert their presence as they rooted for party supremo Akhilesh Yadav cheering loudly and waving the Party flag. Yadav delivered a fiery speech shooting sharply at Modi saying, "Jo UP sey aayey they woh UP sey hi jayengey". He also raised the issue of "chanda chori" from Ram Temple Trust in Ayodhya.Reflecting on the INDIA campaign so far, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya was the first speaker who set the set the tone by highlighting how the parties in the Alliance have unitedly taken up and build the outreach on the issue of SIR and working of Election Commission under CEC Gyanesh Kumar."We took the decision to hit the streets on Sept 30 at the INDIA bloc meeting and since then the slogan of "vote chor gaddi chhod" and "vote bachao, desh bachao" has resonated across the country. Since they started SIR in Bihar people have suffered and faced its impact and to counter it and the autocratic working of the Central govt, the people have responded with this "jan sailaab" he highlighted. Bhattacharya and CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby referred to the ongoing protests as nothing short of a second freedom struggle.RJD's Tejashwi Yadav chose to draw from the epic Mahabharat to make his point. "Vote chori key liyey Mahabharat ka ayojan kiya Hai Ramlila Maidan mein..," he said in Hindi. He cited the example of Shakuni and his dice to highlight that there was a lack of a level-playing field there and alleged that the same situation existed in the Modi regime with Gyanesh Kumar as CEC. He demanded that Gyanesh Kumar should be tried for treason. Rahul Gandhi had raised this at the public impeachment on Saturday and reiterated the same on Sunday.Interestingly, TMC chairperson and former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee while delivering a fiery attack on CEC Gyanesh Kumar, was the only speaker who after highlighting the unity in the INDIA bloc, lauded and backed the efforts of the Cockroach Janta Party and Gen Z in taking up issues ranging from concerns in the examination system to SIR and EC related protests.It was interesting to see a large presence of youth with student outfits. The Left linked student wings like AISA, SFI, AISF and Krantkari Yuva Sangathan joined with full fervour alongside the NSUI. One one side there were the Left students groups who chose to break into an impromtu performance amid the crowd as all waited for the INDIA leaders to arrive. Then one saw a large group of ethnically dressed women and men from Jharkhand play their traditional instruments.An RJD supporter was busy singing patriotic songs, and then there was a stir as one man arrived drenched in sculpted clay depicting Mahatma Gandhi holding the Constitution. There were others too holding cutouts and impressions from the Constitution.Posters calling for Gyanesh Kumar's ouster in Gen Z lingo - "It's done Bro!" and a young man holding up a cutout of BR Ambedkar which read "Ab toh Ungli Uthegi" to a group of men who came wearing a garland of plastic fingers with red stains to symbolise the loss of the voting rights - the rally saw people convey the political message on the importance of voting rights with creative zeal.
Article Summary: The Ramlila Maidan on Sunday became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt. The RJD and Samajwadi Party flags shared space with a sea of flags representing the Left parties - a reflection of how diverse ideologies and ideas converged on ground for a common cause.

Article Title: J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
Article Text:
Article 370, Waqf, BJP: Mehdi explains why he is quitting NC and challenging its ideology

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BUDGAM: At the entrance of the National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi home’s two large banners at the gate sum up the message he wants to convey. One reads, “Wada kursi se bada hai” (a promise is bigger than a chair), while the other says, “Kirdar ki siyasat, usoolon ki siyasat” (politics of character, politics of principles).Inside the hall, party workers gathered in small groups, discussing the fallout of Mehdi's announcement that he would formally resign from as NC MP at a rally here on November 3 on the death anniversary of his father. One worker said, “even at a barber's shop, people do not give up their chairs for someone else even if that person is older. Here is a man willing to leave his chair for the sake of principles. Who gives up a chair like that. ”Inside in his room, sitting calmly in his chair, Mehdi insists his decision to part ways with the party is final and there is no going back.“I have been part of this NC for 24 years. I joined it believing that it stood for autonomy and the rights of the people of J&K. But after the abrogation of Article 370 , whatever remnants of autonomy we had were taken away and the party despite getting a strong mandate in the 2024 Assembly elections on the promise of challenging the status quo, failed to honour it,” Mehdi told the TOI, accusing the chief minister Omar Abdullah of diluting his electoral position on Article 370, Waqf Amendment Act, Muslim issues, reservations and moving closer to the BJP, “to the point of submission.”In the room, hanging on the wall was a large photograph of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, a prominent Shia cleric and Congress leader who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.“I understand it will be long fight but I am not afraid," he said, hastily added that whenever the NC faced an ideological challenge, it found it tough to defend its position. The People’s Democratic Party (PDP) managed, he said, for a brief period, to offer it such a challenge before joining an alliance with the BJP in 2015 reduced party to three members today. “There was also an ideological contest between the NC and the Hurriyat Conference in Jammu and Kashmir for many years. I am not endorsing the Hurriyat Conference as it represented the other extreme. But when it came to ideological contestation, the streets were dominated by the other side, not the National Conference,” he said.He said people need to replace traditional political forces like NC and PDP and other like them with more potent one having conviction. “The common problem with these two political parties and others like them, is their lack of character. It is what they have in common. People trusted the NC and the PDP. But they delivered the same kind of results,” he added.Mehdi, who has been critical of the CM and his government, said the chief minister normalised the post-abrogation arrangement through his government, Assembly and other constitutional institutions. “The party began speaking the very language that the BJP wanted people across the country to speak after the abrogation of Article 370,” he said. He said he found further clarity after NC president Farooq Abdullah recently said in an interview that if Mehdi believed what he says he was free to resign from the party.“Referring to me Dr Abdullah said that if I believed Article 370 could be restored, I was free to move out and get it restored. Effectively, he was saying that he himself did not believe Article 370 could not be restored. This again raises the question, if he does not believe it can be restored constitutionally, why people of Jammu and Kashmir were given the assurance during the poll campaign. In the same interview, he asked me to resign from the party as, in his view, I had become an irritant in the process of normalising the post-abrogation status quo. They wanted me to leave the party because I am questioning their position,” he added.Mehdi also rejected the claim that the NC alone was responsible for his victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Srinagar. “The NC never crossed 1.5 lakh votes in this parliamentary constituency in 30 to 40 years. This time I got nearly 3.80 lakh votes. The bulk of the support came from people in South Kashmir who were not associated with the NC,” he said as number of areas of South Kashmir’s Pulwama and Shopian were added to Srinagar in the delimitation exercise of 2023. He, however, said that he contested on the NC ticket and used the party's name and symbol, making his resignation necessary as he sought to distance himself from the organisation.Mehdi, who is also a prominent shia leader, said he was reaching out to people from different walks of life, including journalists, lawyers, doctors and teachers, to build a credible political alternative.“I am looking for people with no baggage, who have conviction and are willing to walk this path,” he said, adding that the structure and name of any new organisation would be decided later.He said he might contest future by-elections from Srinagar constituency as an independent candidate but insisted his decision to resign was not driven by electoral ambition. “I am not bargaining with people over what I will get in return for resigning. This has nothing to do with electoral results or how people behave. It is a call of conscience and a matter of principles,” he said.
Article Summary: National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi resigns from party. Mehdi accuses Omar Abdullah of diluting his electoral position on Article 370, Waqf Amendment Act, Muslim issues, reservations and moving closer to the BJP.

Article Text:

For many Indians, the day begins with a cup of milky chai, followed by breakfast cooked in ghee. Lunch may come with a bowl of curd and paneer on the menu, while a Sunday meal is often incomplete without chicken curry.These familiar food habits are so deeply woven into everyday life that giving up all animal-derived products can seem like a difficult choice.But for people who turn vegan, the change goes beyond replacing meat with vegetables. It means rethinking everyday ingredients, from milk and butter to honey, as well as choices involving clothing, cosmetics and other products.“There are alternatives for practically everything. You can make curd at home using plant milk, use tofu instead of paneer, and use different nut and soy milks,” says Sarahana, who has been vegan since 2018.On World Vegan Day, observed on November 1, the question is not just why people choose veganism, but what it takes to follow the lifestyle.According to The Vegan Society, veganism is a way of living that seeks to exclude, as far as possible and practicable, all forms of animal exploitation and cruelty.While a vegan diet avoids meat, fish, eggs, dairy and honey, the lifestyle also extends to products made from animals, those tested on animals and activities that use animals for entertainment.For some, the decision is rooted in animal welfare; for others, environmental concerns or health considerations play a role.But the experiences of vegans show that the transition is as much about changing everyday habits as it is about changing one's perspective.India has a long tradition of vegetarian food, but veganism goes a step further by excluding all animal-derived products, including milk, curd, ghee, paneer and honey.According to estimates compiled by World Population Review, around 9% of India's population followed a vegan diet in 2021, amounting to an estimated 121.5 million people. The country also has a substantial vegetarian population, reflecting its diverse food traditions.However, the figure should be treated as an estimate rather than a definitive count, as veganism surveys often rely on self-reported responses and vary in methodologies.A vegan diet does not necessarily mean giving up familiar Indian food or relying on expensive, imported alternatives. Dal, rice, roti, rajma, chole, idli, dosa, poha, upma and vegetable dishes can all be part of a vegan diet, provided they are prepared without animal-derived ingredients.Utkarsh Garg, a representative of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA), says their meals are a mix of familiar Indian dishes and plant-based alternatives.“Breakfast is usually a protein smoothie bowl or soaked oats, although I’m definitely not above a plate of poha, chhole-kulche or one enormous aloo paratha when the mood strikes!”“Lunch and dinner usually include things like tofu, soybeans, dals, rajma and plenty of vegetables. My current obsession is tempeh. I seem to be finding increasingly creative excuses to put it into everything I eat.”“As for living without milk, paneer, curd or ghee, I genuinely don’t find it difficult anymore. There are so many vegan alternatives available now, and many things are surprisingly easy and inexpensive to make at home as well.” Utkarsh said.Sarahana says she relies largely on everyday Indian food rather than packaged substitutes.“As for food, my everyday diet is actually quite simple and Indian. Dal, rice, roti, vegetables, chickpeas, rajma, seasonal produce and different legumes. There are so many naturally plant-based foods available in India. You don’t need expensive imported alternatives or packaged vegan products to survive without dairy.“There are alternatives for practically everything. You can make curd at home using plant milk, use tofu instead of paneer, and use different nut and soy milks. Ghee is essentially clarified butter, and personally, I don’t feel the need to replace it.”The distinction is important. A vegan diet does not require a direct substitute for every non-vegan food. It can instead be built around naturally plant-based ingredients that are already widely used in Indian kitchens.For Utkarsh, the decision began in childhood. Watching a chicken being slaughtered made them connect the food on their plate with the animal it came from. He turned vegetarian that day and later went vegan.“For me, veganism has always been about animals. I’ve loved animals for as long as I can remember. While most kids my age were watching Cartoon Network or Pogo, I was glued to National Geographic, completely fascinated by dogs, cats, cows, snakes, and pretty much every animal I came across,” Utkarsh said.As he learnt more about animal exploitation, vegetarianism no longer felt enough. “My love for animals naturally led me to veganism. I’ve been vegan for four years now, and honestly, it is one of the best decisions I have ever made. More than changing what I eat or wear, it has changed the way I look at the world and my place in it.”For Sarahana, the turning point came in 2018, when she watched a video of a pregnant cow being slaughtered after she was no longer productive for the dairy industry.“My decision came from questioning something very basic: why do we, as human beings, consider ourselves superior to other animals? Why do we love some animals, consider some family, see some as entertainment, and others as food?” she said.While studying gender, Sarahana began drawing parallels between the exploitation of women's bodies and that of female animals in the dairy industry.“How can I study feminism, gender and the exploitation of female bodies and not extend that understanding beyond human beings? How can I talk about patriarchy and exploitation while continuing to pay an industry that repeatedly impregnates female animals, takes away their babies and exploits their reproductive systems?” she said.Coming from a Dalit community, Sarahana also views veganism through the lens of social justice, questioning how societies decide whose lives are valued.“We love cats and dogs, welcome them into our homes and call them family, but we look at chickens, goats and buffaloes and see food. We have created categories of animals that deserve affection and animals that can be exploited,” she added.One common perception is that veganism is an expensive lifestyle, largely because plant-based milk, meat substitutes and other packaged alternatives can cost more than conventional products. However, both Utkarsh and Sarahana say that a vegan diet need not depend on these products.Utkarsh points out that many Indian staples are naturally plant-based. “India is one of the easiest places in which to eat vegan, because so much of the food we already know and love either naturally contains no animal-derived ingredients or can be veganised with ridiculously small changes.“Think about dal, rajma, chole, idli, dosa, poha, upma, roti, sabzis, rice dishes and countless regional foods. Veganism doesn’t have to mean buying an expensive imported mock meat or drinking a fancy packaged plant milk every morning. Those products are great if you enjoy them, but they aren’t what veganism depends on.”Sarahana agrees that the bigger challenge is often social rather than financial.“I don’t think being vegan in India is inherently expensive. Our traditional food already has so many affordable plant-based options. What can become expensive is the packaged vegan alternatives, not the basic diet itself. The bigger challenge is social conditioning. At family gatherings, weddings or even casual conversations, you constantly have to explain why you don’t consume something that everyone else considers normal. ”Both say their families initially had questions and reservations. Utkarsh says their family is now supportive and has started incorporating more vegan foods and products into their lives. Sarahana, meanwhile, says she continues to face comments that she has been “brainwashed”.Veganism is often associated with better health, but a plant-based diet is not automatically a balanced one. Its nutritional value depends on the foods included and whether essential nutrients are adequately supplied.Dt Gausiya Aziz, consultant and head of nutrition and dietetics at SPARSH Hospital, Yelahanka, says a well-planned vegan diet can support cardiovascular and metabolic health.“Research suggests that plant-based dietary patterns rich in fibre, antioxidants and unsaturated fats can help lower LDL cholesterol, improve blood pressure and support healthy weight management. They may also reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes,” she says.However, claims that veganism automatically prevents cancer, reverses chronic diseases or guarantees a longer life are exaggerated, she cautions. Health outcomes depend on overall diet quality, lifestyle and individual medical conditions.A key concern is meeting nutritional requirements. Vitamin B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc, omega-3 fatty acids and protein need particular attention.Vitamin B12 is especially important because reliable natural plant-based sources are limited. Fortified foods or supplements may therefore be necessary.Aziz recommends a varied diet containing whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruits, nuts and seeds, along with appropriate supplementation and regular nutritional assessment.Utkarsh says he pay close attention to their nutritional needs and take vitamin B12 supplements.“I am also quite particular about my nutrition. I take my B12 regularly and pay attention to vitamin D and other essential nutrients. B12 supplementation is important for vegans, and these supplements are accessible at pharmacies,” he said.The PETA representative added that he has noticed less bloating since turning vegan and feel healthier, but stresses that dietary planning matters.“Of course, I think any diet needs to be properly planned rather than treated as automatically healthy simply because it carries a particular label. For me, veganism has actually made me more conscious of what I eat and what my body needs.”Aziz also warns that highly processed vegan foods are not necessarily healthy. Packaged snacks, meat substitutes and desserts can contain high amounts of sodium, refined carbohydrates, added sugars and saturated fats. She advises prioritising minimally processed foods and checking nutritional labels.“Children, pregnant women and older adults have specific nutritional requirements that demand careful consideration before adopting a vegan diet. During childhood, adequate energy, protein, calcium, iron, vitamin B12 and vitamin D are essential for growth and development. Pregnant women must additionally ensure sufficient folate, iodine, choline and omega-3 fatty acids to support maternal health and fetal development. Older adults should prioritise protein intake, calcium and vitamin D to preserve muscle strength and bone health. Vitamin B12 supplementation is particularly important across these groups,” Aziz added.Nutritionist Aziz also recommends consulting a qualified dietitian or healthcare professional before making significant dietary changes.Animal welfare is not the only reason people choose veganism. Environmental concerns are also part of the conversation.Aziz says vegan diets generally have a lower environmental footprint than diets containing substantial amounts of animal products, particularly red meat and dairy.Plant-based food production typically requires less agricultural land and generates fewer greenhouse gas emissions than livestock farming. It can also reduce pressure on biodiversity and freshwater resources.However, the environmental impact varies with farming methods, transportation, processing and food waste. Choosing locally available, seasonal and minimally processed plant foods can help reduce the footprint further.For Utkarsh, the values behind veganism are also connected to ideas of compassion and non-violence.“We grow up hearing about ahimsa and vasudhaiva kutumbakam, the idea that the world is one family. To me, animals shouldn’t be excluded from that circle of compassion simply because they belong to another species,” he said.Going vegan involves more than changing what is on the plate. It can mean checking product labels, asking about ingredients when eating out and finding alternatives to everyday items.Some medications and personal-care products may also contain animal-derived ingredients, making it important to check rather than assume that a product is vegan.For someone considering the transition, Utkarsh suggests starting by understanding where everyday products come from.“For anyone considering going vegan because they care about animals, I would say: start by looking. Look honestly at where our milk, meat, eggs, leather, wool, silk, cosmetics and entertainment come from.”“Once I did that, veganism stopped feeling like something I was ‘giving up’. It started feeling like the most natural extension of something I had believed all along.”Sarahana says the idea is to extend compassion beyond the animals people traditionally consider companions or pets.She also points to the growing number of Indian businesses offering vegan alternatives. For her, such businesses are helping make animal-free choices more accessible.For those thinking of making the switch, the practical starting point may be simple: understand what a vegan diet excludes, plan for essential nutrients and explore the plant-based foods already available in the kitchen.World Vegan Day was established in 1994 by Louise Wallis, then president of The Vegan Society, to mark the 50th anniversary of the organisation's founding in November 1944.The day is now observed annually on November 1 to raise awareness about veganism and its ethical, environmental and health-related aspects.
Article Summary: World Vegan Day is observed annually on November 1. India has a long tradition of vegetarian food, but veganism goes a step further by excluding all animal- derived products. Around 9% of India's population followed a vegan diet in 2021, amounting to 121.5 million people.

Article Title: CBI extradites Mahadev App kingpin Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman
Article Text:
CBI has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman

NEW DELHI: In a major breakthrough against transnational organized crime, CBI in coordination with other Central agencies, has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, the promoter and alleged kingpin of the Mahadev App illegal online betting syndicate, from the Sultanate of Oman.A special CBI team travelled to Muscat, took custody of Chandrakar, and escorted him back to India. Following a mandatory medical examination and the acquisition of a transit remand, he will be taken to Raipur and produced before the CBI Special Judge Monday.Chandrakar is wanted in two CBI cases, in which chargesheets have already been filed, as well as an Enforcement Directorate (ED) case where a prosecution complaint has been submitted and several properties in India and abroad have been attached.The investigation into the Mahadev Online Book cases was taken up by the CBI at the request of the Chhattisgarh government.The probe revealed that the syndicate operated as one of the country's largest illegal online betting networks run from outside India, facilitating unlawful betting on cricket, football, card games, and other events through a widespread system of franchised "panels" and "branches."Proceeds from the illegal betting network were funneled through numerous mule bank accounts, layered via multiple transactions, and moved overseas through hawala channels.CBI investigations also established that a portion of the illicit funds was used to pay protection money to public servants to ensure the unhindered operation of the syndicate.Chargesheets in the matter have been filed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, provisions of the Indian Penal Code relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating, and forgery, as well as the Chhattisgarh Gambling (Prohibition) Act, with Chandrakar named as a key accused.Chandrakar was initially located and detained by the Royal Oman Police following a Red Corner Notice issued against him. Subsequent extradition proposals, accompanied by gathered evidence, were submitted by the CBI and ED, and pursued in close coordination with Indian government agencies, the Interpol National Central Bureau, and Omani authorities.The CBI expressed gratitude to the Government of the Sultanate of Oman and the Royal Oman Police for their cooperation, highlighting the strong bilateral relations and mutual commitment to combating international crime. The extradition represents a key milestone in India's ongoing efforts to hold foreign-based fugitives accountable under Indian law, CBI said.
Article Summary: Sourabh Chandrakar is the promoter and alleged kingpin of the Mahadev App illegal online betting syndicate. He is wanted in two CBI cases, in which chargesheets have already been filed. Chandrakar will be taken to Raipur and produced before the CBI Special Judge Monday.

NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc on Sunday held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The rally held over allegations of “vote chori”, saw senior INDIA bloc leaders accuse the BJP of electoral manipulation and undermining democratic institutions.Several opposition leaders targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission was favouring the ruling party.They demanded Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of trying to influence the West Bengal elections and vowed to fight against the alleged actions.“Bengal is victim of SIR. We will not spare them, we will fight,” she said, adding, “Gyanesh, when will you vanish?”Mamata also accused the BJP of looting funds linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi and Waqf properties, and alleged that the police had become the party's “comrades”.“What haven't they looted? They looted the money of Ram Janmabhoomi, Waqf properties... The police became their comrades. The BJP has no organisation of its own. That is why they make the police do party work. Agencies don't work with the BJP. The BJP will go,” she said.Accusing the BJP of undermining democracy and the Constitution through alleged “vote theft”, Mamata said the party had also deprived young people of jobs, compromised women's dignity and misused donations.“These people have looted the country's democracy and constitution through 'vote theft', and attacked it on top of that. The BJP has stolen youth's jobs, stolen women's honor, stolen donations—we must remove them from power,” she said.“Bengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not give up. We will give our lives, we will fight, but we will not surrender. They looted our Bengal. We will save democracy and bring it back... We will take revenge through politics. We will take revenge through democracy. We will fight...” she added.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission had helped the BJP manipulate elections.“Listen to me. What I say always turns out to be true, doesn't it? I am telling every citizen and every youth of India: Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of Chief Election Commissioner. Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail,” he said.He also alleged that PM Modi and Amit Shah would not have reached their current positions without Kumar's help. “Without Gyanesh Kumar, neither Narendra Modi would have become Prime Minister nor Amit Shah would have become Home Minister,” Rahul said.Rahul said the opposition was not driven by hatred towards the BJP leadership but was fighting to protect the Constitution and the rights of citizens.“We do not hate Narendra Modi, Amit Shah or Gyanesh Kumar. We are people who open the shop of love, not hatred. We are people of non-violence. For me, there is no enemy. Neither Narendra Modi, nor Amit Shah, nor Gyanesh Kumar. But the voice of every citizen of India is more important to me, even more important than religion. That is my religion,” he said.He added that the INDIA bloc would not resort to violence or spread hatred but would continue to oppose any attempt to undermine the Constitution.“We will not use violence, we will not harm anyone and we will not spread hatred. We will work with love. But we will not let you destroy the Constitution. No matter what happens, we will not let it happen,” Rahul said.Rahul also raised concerns over unemployment, farmers' rights and the concentration of wealth, alleging that the country's resources were increasingly in the hands of a few people.“The farmer is not getting his rights. The youth are not getting employment. The labourer is not getting his rights, and the entire wealth has gone into the hands of two or three people. We do not want such an India, and we will not accept such an India,” he said.He said the country should ensure that farmers received the benefits of their hard work and that students who worked hard had access to employment.“Anyone can join Shiv ki Baraat. Every living being can join it. Can anyone be stopped from participating in that? No. We want that kind of India. If a farmer works hard, he should reap the rewards. If a student studies for 18 hours, they should get employment. We do not want a country that belongs only to two or three people,” Rahul said.Referring to Amit Shah's remarks that PM Modi would remain in power, Rahul said the opposition would continue its campaign after demanding action against the CEC.“Amit Shah ji said Narendra Modi is not going anywhere. I am telling you the opposite: Narendra Modi cannot go anywhere. Even if he wants to leave, we will not let him go. After Gyanesh Kumar, we are going to stand right in front of you. Legal action will be taken against them,” he said.Rahul described Kumar's removal as the first step towards putting the country back on the right track. “The first step to get the country back on the right track is to remove Gyanesh Kumar,” he said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged that the BJP government had come to power through a “stolen” mandate. He said removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi was necessary to protect democracy.Kharge accused Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of attempting to take away the voting rights of Dalits, women and young people. He alleged that the two leaders were shielding CEC Gyanesh Kumar.“Modi and Shah have attempted to snatch the vote of Dalits, youth and women. Modi ji wants to take away their votes through his man -- Ganesh Kumar. We will keep fighting until he goes, and ensure his exit,” Kharge said.He further alleged that the BJP-led governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh had been formed through “vote chori”.“Be it the central government, governments in Maharashtra, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, they are 'chori' governments (formed on stolen mandate). We have to throw out these 'vote chor',” he said.Kharge also said the opposition would continue its agitation until Kumar resigned.“No matter how many attempts Narendra Modi makes.. until Gyanesh Kumar resigns, we will not stay silent—we will keep fighting,” he said.He added that opposition leaders would not be intimidated by central agencies or the police.“We have the strength to fight and will not be intimidated by the police, CBI, ED or any other government agency. Neither will our INDIA alliance leaders be scared. Everyone on this stage is ready to fight,” Kharge said.He also reiterated his call for Modi's removal, saying: “Modi jayega to hi loktantra bachega, Modi ko hatayenge tabhi loktantra ko bachenyenge, Modi ko hatao loktantra ko bachao (Remove Modi to save democracy).”Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav described Ramlila Maidan as the “Haldighati of democracy” and said the rally signalled that political change could come at any time.“Today, Ramlila Maidan has turned into the Haldighati of democracy. The massive public support and slogans of revolution are proof that change can happen at any moment,” he said.Akhilesh also targeted the BJP, saying those who had once claimed to be an “unmovable foot of Angad” had lost their political ground.He alleged that the party was turning to the Election Commission because it feared losing elections.“The people of UP know how to welcome and how to bid farewell even better. In 2027, such a farewell will happen that the Bharatiya Janata Party and its allies will not be able to return again,” he added.Jammu & Kashmir National Conference President Farooq Abdullah says, "...Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will remain a part of India. They will not be able to separate it.""These people point fingers at Muslims and call them Pakistanis. I want to tell the BJP and RSS: We have given our blood for India. We gave it in the past, we are giving it today, and we will give it tomorrow. This is Ambedkar's Constitution. This is India's Constitution. We are all equal, and everyone has an equal vote. Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will remain a part of India. They will not be able to separate it," he added.Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav compared the opposition rally to the Mahabharata, accusing those in power of manipulating elections.“While the Ramlila Maidan is traditionally meant for staging the Ramayana, today we have organised a 'Mahabharata' for those who steal votes,” he said.Referring to the dice game in the epic, Tejashwi said, “You are all aware of the game Shakuni played in the Mahabharata. You know your history: the Mahabharata began not on a battlefield, but with a game of dice. And now that Shakuni is playing his game, we are compelled to fight the battle...”Several senior opposition leaders attended the rally, including Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby, CPI general secretary D Raja and CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya.Earlier, INDIA bloc leaders travelled in an open vehicle from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction towards Ramlila Maidan, as hundreds of supporters marched alongside them.
Article Summary: Leaders of the INDIA bloc held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of trying to influence the West Bengal elections.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: "Always worry about": Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi's parenting decision kept their two children away from the pressure of tennis stardom
Article Text:
Meet Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi's children, Jaden and Jaz

Why Jaden and Jaz Agassi never pursued professional tennis

Growing up with two of the greatest tennis players in history could easily make professional sports feel like a family tradition. But Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi had a different vision for their children. Despite building legendary careers and collecting some of tennis' biggest honours, the couple never expected their son, Jaden, and daughter, Jaz, to follow in their footsteps. Instead, they allowed both children to discover their own interests, build separate identities and enjoy childhood without the pressure of living up to their famous surname.Graf and Agassi married in October 2001, shortly before welcoming their first child. Their son, Jaden Gil Agassi, was born on October 26, 2001. Two years later, on October 3, 2003, they welcomed their daughter, Jaz Elle Agassi.Although their parents spent decades competing at the highest level, the children grew up largely away from public attention.Agassi's own childhood played an important role in shaping his parenting approach. In his autobiography,, he described the intense pressure his father placed on him to become a successful tennis player.“My father yells everything twice, sometimes three times, sometimes 10,” he wrote. “Harder, he says, harder. Hit earlier. Damn it Andre, hit earlier, Crowd the ball, crowd the ball.”Having experienced that demanding environment himself, Agassi wanted something different for his children. Graf also made it clear that they were free to choose their own interests.“We never really introduced tennis so much into their lives. They’ve chosen other things,” the mom of two shared.Jaden found his passion in baseball rather than tennis. He joined the University of Southern California in 2019 and played college baseball before gaining experience with summer league teams. In 2025, he also represented Team Germany in the World Baseball Classic Qualifiers.His ambition is to build a sporting identity separate from his parents' achievements.“Agassi is a very tennis last name, of course,” Jaden told WKBN News in June 2024. “The goal is to try to make it a baseball one.”Jaz, meanwhile, has explored dancing and horseback riding. She also enjoys outdoor activities, including snowboarding. Unlike her brother, she keeps much of her personal life away from public attention.Agassi has also spoken openly about protecting his children's freedom to choose their own paths.“The idea that a parent would attach a child’s right to be loved in this world based on their performance is a tragedy,” he explained in a 2024 conversation with USA Today. “What somebody needs to do to be pro at 16 years old is crazy, right?”He once described tennis as an unusual sport and explained why he and Graf avoided pushing their children towards it.“It’s a weird sport,” Andre told Fox Sports. “We don’t see too many second-generation players. For us, it’s about raising our children in a way we can share in their life and not always worry about their life.”For the tennis legends, their children's happiness matters far more than another championship trophy.
Article Summary: Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi have two children, Jaden and Jaz. The couple never expected their children to follow in their footsteps. They allowed both children to discover their own interests and build separate identities. Agassi has spoken openly about protecting his children's freedom to choose their own paths.

Article Title: Atlanta Hawks rookie faces suspension after controversial elbow to opponent sparks disciplinary action

The NBA has suspended Atlanta Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings for one game without pay. The league says the guard intentionally elbowed New Orleans Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head during Saturday’s 121-99 loss. It happened with 3:04 left in the fourth quarter. Officials gave Flemings a technical foul and ejected the rookie, and a short scuffle followed in which New Orleans’ Julian Reese also drew a technical. Flemings will miss Monday’s road game against the Indiana Pacers, a night when the Hawks already have four players listed as questionable or out.The league ruled the contact was deliberate and said the elbow landed on McGowens’ head. The 19-year-old threw it while running back up the floor, and the whistle came fast. A review ended with the ejection.Flemings had 12 points, six assists and two rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench before the ejection. The No. 8 pick in the 2026 draft out of Houston is averaging 7.1 points, 4.7 assists and 2.9 rebounds this season. The suspension costs the guard one game check, and Flemings is due back Wednesday against the Washington Wizards.Flemings is the only true point guard on the roster, so the gap is hard to fill. The rookie was coming off the best game of his young career, with 23 points, five assists and five rebounds against Miami last Wednesday. The injury report came out Monday, and the suspension followed shortly after, which left Atlanta little time to adjust.Aaron Wiggins is expected to take heavier minutes. Two-way guard RayJ Dennis could get first regular-season action. Dennis has played well in the G League for Atlanta, but NBA minutes are a different test.The frontcourt is the bigger problem. Jock Landale, Mouhamed Gueye and Henri Veesaar are out, and Jalen Johnson is questionable. If Johnson sits, second-year forward Asa Newell should get a larger role. Newell played over 18 minutes Saturday after Landale went down early, finishing with 13 points and four rebounds. Shooting was a struggle, and defense is still a work in progress.Even with Johnson available, Newell likely plays. Rookie Zuby Ejiofor could log first minutes of the season. He took third-center minutes in the preseason but saw little court time, and the question mark is shooting. Dorian Finney-Smith, who has played small-ball center before, is a wildcard.
Article Summary: The NBA has suspended Atlanta Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings for one game without pay. The league says the guard intentionally elbowed New Orleans Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head during Saturday’s 121-99 loss. Article Title: 'We don't play enough T20': Gautam Gambhir asks players to 'stay in shape' after New Zealand series

India head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked his players to maintain their fitness and continue working on their game during a month-long break from T20I cricket after India completed a 3-2 series win over New Zealand.India won the first three matches to take an unassailable lead in the five-match series, but New Zealand bounced back by winning the final two games at home.Addressing the players in the dressing room after the fifth T20I, Gambhir praised their efforts, pointing to the limited preparation time and the challenge of playing in unfamiliar conditions."You can be extremely proud of the effort that you guys have put in throughout the series. Winning the series, especially when you had just one day to prepare and were playing against a quality team like New Zealand in their own backyard, is a terrific achievement. You should be extremely proud," Gambhir told the players.India also had to deal with a few setbacks during the series. Ishan Kishan missed two matches due to an injury concern, while the bowling attack included relatively inexperienced players Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav, who were making their first appearances in New Zealand.Gambhir said India had set the tone for the rest of the tour and urged the ODI and Test teams to build on the T20I side's performance."You can go back with your heads held high. We wanted to win the last two games as well, but sometimes these things happen. I thought you guys have set the tone for the rest of the tour. Before the start of the series, I said that you had the responsibility to set the tone. Now, it is up to the ODI and Test teams to continue from where you have left off," he said.India's next T20I assignment will be a three-match home series against Sri Lanka in December. The squad will have roughly a month away from international T20 cricket, but Gambhir asked the players to use the break to stay fit and prepare for the next series."We know that we don't play enough T20 cricket, and we've got a month off now. So, make sure we stay in shape and prepare well for Sri Lanka," he said.The India coach also told the players not to become complacent after the series win and stressed the need to keep improving as a team."We can't take any opposition lightly. We have to continue growing as a team, thinking as a team and playing as a team," Gambhir added.India will now shift their focus to the ODI and Test assignments against New Zealand, while the T20I squad will regroup ahead of the Sri Lanka series in December.
Article Summary: India coach Gautam Gambhir tells players to stay fit during month-long break from T20I cricket. India completed a 3-2 series win over New Zealand after winning the first three matches. India's next assignment will be a three-match home series against Sri Lanka in December.

India's long wait for a maiden Women's World Cup title ended on November 2, 2025, when Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai. The victory remains a landmark moment for Indian women's cricket and women's sport in India.The win, in front of a packed stadium, brought an end to a campaign that had nearly slipped away after India suffered three consecutive defeats in the league stage, including one against South Africa.There were several reasons why this World Cup meant so much to India. They were playing at home, had emerged as one of the formidable teams in women's cricket and had pushed Australia, the dominant force in the game, harder than anyone else. India had also beaten Australia in the semi-final to book their place in the title clash. After years of coming close, the team finally had a chance to win the trophy.India's triumph was set up by two players who delivered when it mattered most. Shafali Verma, who was not part of the original squad and came in as a replacement ahead of semi-final after Pratika Rawal was ruled out with an ankle injury, scored 87 off 78 balls in the final.Her innings helped India post 298 for 7. She also took two wickets at a crucial stage of South Africa's chase.Deepti Sharma played an equally important role. The off-spinner, who had also improved her batting, scored a half-century at a run-a-ball before taking five wickets. She combined her ability to generate turn with the control needed to restrict South Africa. India eventually won by 52 runs, though the margin did not reflect how closely contested the final was.Both teams had experienced heartbreak in the past, but only one could lift the trophy. South Africa were left disappointed, particularly their captain Laura Wolvaardt, who finished as the tournament's highest run-scorer. After scoring a century in the semi-final, she produced another fine innings in the final. As long as she was at the crease, South Africa remained in contention, given the depth in their batting line-up. Her innings ended when she was dismissed for 101 off 98 balls, miscuing a shot off Deepti into the night sky.Nadine de Klerk, who had helped South Africa beat India in the league stage, kept the chase alive with her hitting. But with 78 runs still needed and only the last two batters left to support her, the task proved too difficult.South Africa had won the toss, which appeared to be an advantage given the dew usually present during evening matches in Navi Mumbai. However, the expected dew did not arrive. Rain had delayed the start by two hours, bringing temperatures down before nightfall and reducing the impact of the conditions on the teams.That left both sides playing on similar terms. India had more batters in form who could rotate the strike against spin without taking unnecessary risks, while their spinners posed a greater threat. As long as the conditions remained free of dew, Deepti and Shree Charani had the advantage on a pitch where the ball tended to stop and turn. Chasing 299 was always going to be difficult for South Africa.India's total was the second-highest in the history of Women's World Cup finals. Yet, considering what had happened in the semi-final at the same venue, when India defeated Australia while chasing 339, and the depth in South Africa's batting, 298 did not appear to be an insurmountable target.The scale of India's achievement became clearer as they began defending the total. With 11 overs remaining, South Africa needed 92 runs with five wickets in hand. Wolvaardt was keeping them in the contest, but her dismissal changed the course of the match. Amanjot Kaur took a brilliant catch in the deep to send the South African captain back, allowing India to take control.South Africa were eventually bowled out for 246 in the 46th over.The final went deep into the night, but when Harmanpreet took the catch at extra cover to dismiss Nadine de Klerk and seal the 52-run victory, the DY Patil Stadium erupted.Pratika Rawal, who was celebrating with the team in a wheelchair after her injury, had a smile. After years of waiting, India had finally won the Women's World Cup.
Article Summary: India's long wait for a maiden Women's World Cup title ended on November 2, 2025. Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final. The victory remains a landmark moment for Indian women's cricket and women's sport in India.

Garage Beer builds customer loyalty through community and creativity

Garage Beer is taking an unconventional route to win over beer drinkers, and Jason Kelce is right at the centre of its strategy. Rather than compete with major brewing companies through expensive advertising, the independent brand is turning ridiculous jokes, unexpected stunts and genuine fan connections into its biggest marketing assets. In March 2026, the company is showing how a distinctive personality can help a smaller business capture attention. Its approach is simple: entertain people first, build a community around the experience and let the brand become part of the conversation.Garage Beer's latest marketing push arrived ahead of March Madness, with college basketball commentator and lawyer Jay Bilas taking on the fictional role of its 'Attorney at Lager'. The campaign pokes fun at local law firm advertisements, complete with a video commercial and a hotline where fans can leave messages. The brand also introduced a sweepstakes offering a $5,000 TickPick gift card.However, the campaign reflects a much bigger creative strategy. Garage Beer has built its identity around humour that established competitors might hesitate to embrace. Its regional Super Bowl advertisement offered a memorable example, with co-owner Jason Kelce putting horse manure on his face while parodying Budweiser's famous Clydesdale commercials.Chief Creative Officer Corey Smale believes this unconventional approach gives the company an advantage.“Dumb is hard to replicate,” said Garage Beer Chief Creative Officer Corey Smale. “The authenticity that the brand has put out there over the last few years is uniquely ours. We have to stay committed to that.”The company has also introduced a weekly Instagram series called 'Thank Garage It's Friday'. Featuring fictional laboratory experiments, bizarre inventions and mock press conferences, the videos aim to give audiences something entertaining amid the endless stream of social media content.Garage Beer's response to its Super Bowl advertisement also revealed how quickly it can adapt. Although the team expected its toilet humour to attract attention, viewers became more interested in the miniature horse featured in the commercial. The brand responded with merchandise, stickers and a farm experience sweepstakes centred on the animal.Beyond social media, Garage Beer is investing in physical merchandise and experiences that bring its online community closer to the brand. Its products are now available across all 50 states, giving the company a wider platform for future launches.Smale also revealed that the brand relies on a small in-house creative team rather than traditional advertising agencies. It has created a private Instagram group for around 5,000 dedicated followers, allowing the company to test ideas and gather reactions before wider releases.One unusual example involved a loyal customer who repeatedly posted about the brand and jokingly asked Garage Beer to buy him a house. Smale sent him $500 through Venmo, and the follower later shared photographs of his new home.The gesture captures the unusual relationship Garage Beer wants with its customers. Instead of treating fans as just another audience, the company wants them to become active supporters who help shape its identity.As the March 2026 campaign demonstrates, Garage Beer is betting that personality, humour and genuine community connections can compete with advertising budgets that smaller brands simply cannot match.

Article Title: Shaheen Afridi pleads guilty as Pakistan punished after tri-series win; Babar advised to 'go to Australia' amid poor form
Article Text:

Yousuf advises struggling Babar to 'go to Australia'

Pakistan men's cricket team on Monday were fined five per cent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during the Final of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday.The hosts were found to be one over short after time allowances were taken into consideration by Match Referee Jeff Crowe."Their breach was in accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time," the ICC said in a statement.On field umpires Ahsan Raza and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid, and fourth umpire Rashid Riaz levelled the charge.Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pled guilty to the slow over-rate offence and accepted the proposed sanction, the ICC release further said.The fine comes after Pakistan registered a thrilling three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka to lift the tri-series trophy in front of their home crowd.Chasing a huge target of 326, the hosts reached 331 for seven with nine balls remaining, completing the tournament-winning run chase. Fakhar Zaman was the chief architect of Pakistan’s successful pursuit, scoring 127 off 99 deliveries, his 12th ODI century. He received valuable support from Saad Baig, who scored 74 off 75 balls, as the pair rescued the hosts after early dismissals of Maaz Sadaqat (5 off 7) and Babar Azam (0 off 5).With Pakistan needing late impetus after Zaman’s dismissal, Arafat Minhas delivered a decisive contribution, smashing 61 off just 31 deliveries, including four sixes and as many boundaries. His aggressive knock brought the equation within reach before Shaheen sealed the victory with a six.Earlier, Kamindu Mendis had struck 131, while Pavan Rathnayake contributed 77, taking Sri Lanka to 325 for eight. However, their efforts proved insufficient as Pakistan completed the chase to claim the tri-series title.Meanwhile, former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf on Sunday advised star Pakistan batter Babar Azam to travel to Australia or South Africa and seek specialised help to address the technical flaws in his batting, saying playing first-class cricket alone may not be enough to resolve his prolonged slump.Babar's struggles came into focus again during Pakistan's big run chase against Sri Lanka in the tri-series final on Saturday, as he failed to make a significant contribution despite his team's triumph in the tournament."He should be going to South Africa or Australia and just focusing on working on his batting now. That will help him," Yousuf said in a post on social media on Sunday, as quoted by news agency PTI.Babar, who has scored just one century in the last three years in one-day internationals, will be leading Pakistan in the two Test series against Sri Lanka from 9 November but serious doubts have arisen over his place in the white ball squads.The 32-year-old, who has 20 hundreds in ODIs, has already been dropped from the T20 format and if he is to make Pakistan’s squad for next year’s World Cup he will have to show a big reversal in form and attitude in his batting.He has also opted to play a first-class match for Lahore in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, which begins on November 3, to prepare for the upcoming Test series.
Article Summary: Pakistan men's cricket team fined five per cent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during the Final of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series against Sri Lanka. The fine comes after Pakistan registered a thrilling three- wicket victory over Sri Lanka to lift the tri-series trophy in front of their home crowd.

Article Title: First time since 2020, Russia's flag and national anthem return to Olympics as IOC eases restrictions
Article Text:
Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games - Opening Ceremony - Abdoulaye Wade Stadium, Diamniadio, Senegal - October 31, 2026 Russia athletes during the opening ceremony

Youth Olympics open in Senegal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Russia has returned to the Olympic stage with its national flag and anthem for the first time since 2020, with 13 athletes competing at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal. The return comes after six years of restrictions linked to the country's doping scandal and Ukraine war.Russian athletes had been required to compete under neutral identities at subsequent Olympic events. They were not allowed to represent their country through its flag, anthem or national symbols. However, the arrangement has changed at the Youth Olympics, which opened on Saturday, October 31.The development follows a gradual easing of restrictions by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 2026. In July, the IOC provisionally lifted the suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee and withdrew its recommendations restricting the participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes in international competitions. Individual sports federations, however, continue to decide which athletes are eligible to compete.Ukraine has not boycotted sporting events in which Russian athletes have participated. Boycotts were once a common feature of international sport, with three successive Summer Olympics, from 1976 to 1984, affected by them.In the latter two cases, the IOC was more affected than the intended targets.The Youth Olympic Games opened in Senegal on Saturday, marking the first Olympic event to be held in Africa. The Games are also part of the continent's efforts to play a bigger role in international sport.Tens of thousands of spectators attended the opening ceremony at the Diamniadio Olympic Stadium, near the capital Dakar. Hundreds of drummers and dancers showcased Senegalese and African culture under the Games motto, “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates.”Performers dressed in yellow, black and white traditional Senegalese gowns came together to form a giant map of Africa. The ceremony also featured West African oral storytelling, concerts by Senegalese singers and the athletes' parade.Around 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 will compete across Dakar, nearby Diamniadio and the beach resort of Saly until November 13.Russia's 13-member contingent is competing under its national flag for the first time at an Olympic event since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 led to its suspension.The Games will also feature the first refugee team at a Youth Olympics. The six athletes, based in Kenya and Uganda, will compete in track and field, judo and taekwondo.Athletes will compete for medals across 153 events in 25 sports. Singapore hosted the first Summer Youth Olympic Games in 2010. Dakar was originally scheduled to host the event in 2022, but the coronavirus pandemic led to its postponement.Africa has hosted several major international sporting events in recent years. South Africa became the first African country to host the FIFA World Cup in 2010, while Morocco will co-host the 2030 tournament with Spain and Portugal. Rwanda hosted the continent's first road cycling world championships last year, and Formula 1 is set to return to Africa with a Grand Prix in Rwanda early next decade. Botswana also hosted the World Athletics Relays in May.
Article Summary: Russia's 13-member contingent is competing under its national flag for the first time at an Olympic event since 2020. The return comes after six years of restrictions linked to the country's doping scandal and Ukraine war. The Youth Olympic Games opened in Senegal on Saturday, marking the first Olympic event to be held in Africa.

Article Title: India vs New Zealand: Shubman Gill turns up the volume at Eden Park; Virat Kohli opts for gym, Rohit Sharma stays indoors

Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma (BCCI Photo)

No nets for Kohli; Rohit skips session too

AUCKLAND: Volume has always been the keyword when it comes to Shubman Gill 's preparations for a fixture. Whether it is the IPL, ODIs or Tests, there is no compromise on the number of deliveries he faces, the sprints he completes or the big hits he unleashes.It was no different on Monday at Eden Park, where the India captain had another marathon net session. It began with gentle throwdowns and culminated in an extended fielding session with spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule. For close to three hours, Gill, who had skipped Sunday's session, made the most of the morning and ensured he reached his desired workload.While fast bowlers Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi were given a breather after bowling lengthy spells the previous day, a combination of local spinners and fast bowlers worked hard to provide batting practice to Gill and KL Rahul, the only two designated batters to turn up at the nets.The centre wicket remained the focus of most of the action, with Rahul beginning his session by donning the big gloves. The experienced wicketkeeper-batter spent close to 15 minutes collecting throwdowns from Dayanand Garani and Nuwan Seneviratne before padding up to bat alongside Gill.The two batters faced deliveries for close to a minute each before sprinting to the other end to make way for their partner. The drill continued as Bahutule kept a close eye on proceedings from behind the bowler's arm.A handful of spectators had gathered along the main road near the square boundary, repeatedly calling out, "Gill bhai, autograph dedo, main Moga... Punjab se hu." Even Rahul had to contend with the noise as the two batters remained in high demand, with fans eager to get their autographs, selfies and pictures.Once satisfied with his batting output and after putting on a show with his trademark strokes, particularly the big inside-out drive, Rahul disappeared into the tunnel and did not return.For Gill, however, the job was only half done. Having completed the longest batting session of the day, he wrapped up his workout with catching drills from different positions. After working on close-in and slip catching, he also practised taking high catches near the boundary ropes before calling it a day.Following a quick massage to his neck, which has troubled him of late whenever he ramps up his workload, Gill headed off. The ground staff then switched on the sprinklers to give the square some much-needed recovery after the morning's exertions.By the time Gill and company left for the hotel, the remaining members of the ODI squad would have been close to reaching Auckland from Hamilton, the venue of the fifth T20I. The entire squad will have just one opportunity to train together on Tuesday before the five-match series gets underway on November 4.Nearly an hour into India's training session, a luxury car emerged from the tunnel leading to the dressing rooms. It proceeded towards the main exit before briefly stopping, allowing the passenger to catch a glimpse of the centre wicket, where Rahul and Gill were batting. Virat Kohli was seated in the front seat. The former India captain had completed a gym session at the venue and left without taking part in any batting or fielding drills.Kohli was not the only senior batter to skip the nets. Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad also chose to stay indoors and are expected to fine-tune their preparations alongside the rest of the squad on the eve of the match.India are scheduled to train in the afternoon on Tuesday, while New Zealand will have a morning session.
Article Summary: Shubman Gill and KL Rahul were the only two designated batters to turn up at the nets at Eden Park. Virat Kohli was not the only senior batter to skip the nets. Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad also chose to stay indoors and are expected to fine-tune their preparations.

Afghanistan completed a 3-0 sweep of Zimbabwe in the T20I series after beating them by seven wickets in the third and final match in Sharjah on Sunday. Noor Ahmad led the bowling effort with his maiden five-wicket haul, taking 5/13 in 3.3 overs as Zimbabwe were bowled out for just 79 in under 15 overs.Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran had opted to bowl, hoping to test his team's chasing ability. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Azmatullah Omarzai dismissed openers Innocent Kaia and Brian Bennett in successive overs, before Abdullah Tarakhail removed Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza to leave the visitors struggling at 13/3 in the fourth over.Ryan Burl tried to steady the innings with 30 runs but was dismissed leg before wicket by Abdollah Ahmadzai. Article Title: Luka Doncic gets an early message from Bam Adebayo ahead of Lakers-Heat showdown
Article Text:
Luka Doncic and Bam Adebayo. Image via: Rich Storry/ Getty Images

What did Bam Adebayo say about guarding Luka Doncic?

Can the Lakers hold up when Doncic sits?
